title: The Timeless Art of Traditional Odia Jewellery
excerpt: Discover the rich heritage of Odisha's jewellery traditions — from Tarakasi to Temple jewellery — and how they continue to inspire generations.
content:
Odisha has a jewellery tradition that dates back over 2,000 years, with styles that have been shaped by temple architecture, royal patronage, and the skill of local artisans. The word 'Tarakasi' itself evokes images of delicate silver filigree — a craft that originated in Cuttack and spread across the state, with Balasore emerging as a key centre for this intricate art. Here, molten silver is drawn into threads thinner than a human hair, then curled and twisted into floral patterns, peacocks, and mythological figures.

Pattachitra-inspired jewellery is another uniquely Odia tradition. Borrowing motifs from the cloth paintings of Raghurajpur, this style uses bold outlines, vibrant enamel colours, and symbolic imagery such as the lotus, conch shell, and the divine face of Lord Jagannath. Temple jewellery, on the other hand, draws from the architectural grandeur of the Sun Temple at Konark and the Lingaraja Temple in Bhubaneswar, featuring gopuram-shaped pendants, deity idols, and intricate border work.

What makes Odia jewellery truly special is the philosophy behind it. Jewellery here is not just adornment — it is considered an auspicious asset, a symbol of marital status, a store of wealth, and a medium of artistic expression. From the Jadanagam (gold waist belt) worn by brides to the daily wear thali necklace, each piece carries cultural meaning. At Mahalaxmi Jewellery in Balasore, we are proud to continue these traditions while introducing contemporary designs that keep the heritage alive for the next generation.
author: Anjali Mohapatra

title: A Complete Guide to Buying Hallmarked Gold in India
excerpt: Everything you need to know about BIS hallmarking, gold purity, and how to verify your jewellery before purchasing.
content:
If you are buying gold in India, hallmarking is your guarantee of purity. Since 2021, BIS hallmarking has been mandatory for gold jewellery and artefacts in select districts across the country, and the scope is expanding every year. The hallmark mark comprises four components: the BIS logo, the purity in carats (such as 22K916 for 22-carat gold), the jeweller's identification mark, and the hallmarking centre's mark from a NABL-accredited assaying lab.

But what does this mean for you as a buyer? When you purchase hallmarked jewellery from Mahalaxmi Jewellery, you can be certain that the piece contains exactly 91.6% pure gold in the case of 22K, with the remaining 8.4% being alloy metals like copper and silver that add strength. Without hallmarking, there is no independent verification — some jewellers may sell you 18K gold at 22K prices or mix higher amounts of alloy. Hallmarking eliminates this risk entirely.

Always check for the hallmark on the inside of bangles and rings, or on the clasp of necklaces and chains. Use the BIS Care app to verify the HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) number assigned to each piece. At Mahalaxmi, every gold item above 2 grams comes with BIS hallmarking and a detailed invoice stating the purity, weight, and making charges separately. Never hesitate to ask your jeweller for the hallmark certificate — a trustworthy jeweller will always provide it proudly.

title: The Ultimate Bridal Jewellery Checklist for an Odia Wedding
excerpt: From the Jadanagam to the Chitki — a comprehensive guide to the essential jewellery pieces every Odia bride needs.
content:
An Odia wedding is a deeply traditional affair, and the bride's jewellery is an integral part of the rituals. The must-have pieces start with the Jadanagam (gold waist belt), which is tied around the bride's waist during the wedding ceremony and symbolises prosperity and marital bliss. Next comes the Chitki, a traditional gold necklace set with uncut diamonds and rubies, often featuring a large pendant with deity motifs.

The bride's ears are adorned with Jhumkas or Chandbalis — oversized, temple-inspired earrings that frame the face beautifully. On the hands, a set of gold bangles called Guntha (stacked bangles) are worn, often in odd numbers as per tradition. A Nathani (nose ring) completes the facial adornment, usually in gold with a pearl or kundan drop. The Mangalsutra with black beads and a gold pendant is the most significant piece, as it is tied by the groom and worn for a lifetime.

At Mahalaxmi Jewellery, we recommend brides begin their jewellery shopping at least 3-4 months before the wedding to allow time for custom pieces. Start with the heavier investment pieces like the Chitki and Jadanagam, then layer in the smaller items. Consider coordinating the jewellery with your wedding saree — traditional Odia paata or silk sarees pair beautifully with temple gold. Book a free consultation with our bridal designer in Balasore to create a cohesive trousseau that matches your wedding palette and budget.

title: How to Care for Your Gold Jewellery: Maintenance Tips That Last a Lifetime
excerpt: Learn the dos and don'ts of gold jewellery care to keep your pieces shining for generations.
content:
Gold is a noble metal that does not tarnish or rust, but it does require regular care to maintain its lustre. The number one rule is to store each piece separately. Gold is a soft metal, and when pieces are tossed together in a box, they scratch one another. Use soft cloth pouches or a jewellery box with individual compartments. At Mahalaxmi, we provide a complimentary soft pouch with every purchase to help you store your jewellery safely.

Cleaning your gold jewellery is simple — mix a few drops of mild dish soap with warm water (not hot), soak the piece for 10-15 minutes, then gently scrub with a soft-bristled toothbrush. Pay attention to crevices where dirt and oil accumulate. Rinse with clean water and pat dry with a lint-free cloth. For pieces with gemstones or enamel work, avoid soaking — use a damp cloth instead. Avoid using harsh chemicals, chlorine, or abrasive cleaners, as they can damage the finish and loosen stones.

Remove your jewellery before swimming, bathing, applying lotion, or doing household chores. Chlorine in swimming pools can discolour gold alloys, and chemicals in cleaning products can dull the finish. We recommend getting your jewellery professionally cleaned and inspected at our Balasore showroom once a year — we offer this service free of charge for all our customers. With proper care, your gold jewellery can remain radiant and wearable for decades, becoming a cherished heirloom for your children and grandchildren.

title: Festival Jewellery Trends in Odisha: What's In for Raja and Diwali 2026
excerpt: From oxidised silver for Raja to diamond-studded gold for Diwali — explore the hottest jewellery trends for Odisha's favourite festivals.
content:
Odisha's festival calendar is packed with occasions that call for new jewellery. Raja Sankranti, the three-day festival celebrating womanhood and the earth's fertility, has traditionally been associated with new clothes, swings, and lightweight jewellery. This year, the trend is shifting towards oxidised silver sets with colourful enamel work — think chokers with peacock motifs, layered bead necklaces, and stackable bangles with floral engravings. These pieces are affordable, stylish, and perfect for the festive spirit without being too heavy.

For Diwali, the emphasis is on opulence. Odia families invest heavily in gold during this period, and the trend for Diwali 2026 is diamond-studded gold in contemporary cuts. Princess-cut and cushion-cut diamond necklaces paired with traditional polki jhumkas are proving popular among younger buyers. Temple jewellery with uncut diamonds is also seeing a resurgence, particularly the classic 'Nava Graha' (nine planets) pendants that are considered auspicious for home blessings during the festival of lights.

Durga Puja and Kumar Purnima are all about statement pieces — oversized chandbalis, matha pattis, and heavy gold bangles stacked up to the elbow. The 'more is more' philosophy applies here, and layering is key. At Mahalaxmi in Balasore, our Festival Special collection for 2026 brings together all these trends in one place. We recommend visiting early in the season, as our most popular festival pieces tend to sell out quickly. And remember — festival shopping with our gold savings scheme means you earn bonus gold while you celebrate.
